options.text: A biotic–biotic interaction, because the earthworm and the soil are both treated as living.
A biotic–abiotic interaction, because a living earthworm interacts with non-living soil.
An abiotic–abiotic interaction, because soil and moisture are both non-living.
No interaction, because the earthworm never touches the soil.

stem:
Nidhi watches an earthworm burrow through moist soil. Living parts of a habitat are biotic; non-living parts such as soil and moisture are abiotic.

Which type of habitat interaction is this?

teacher.key_rationale: Earthworm is biotic; soil is abiotic; their interaction is biotic–abiotic. Soil is not living; ignoring the earthworm mis-scopes the pair; burrowing is contact with soil.
